hero.subtext: Investigate Earth's changing systems through long-term satellite observations. From global observations to statistically tested evidence, explore what the data shows — and how strong the evidence is.
hero.integrityBadge: Authentic NASA Earthdata • Non-Parametric Statistics • Traceable Provenance

questions.heading: Four Questions. One Scientific Standard.
questions.subheading: Observed change is only the beginning of the investigation. Every trend is tested against four rigorous inquiries:

q1.title: WHAT IS CHANGING?
q1.desc: Select calibrated physical, hydrological, and vegetative indicators across surface temperature, precipitation, canopy vitality, and water storage.

q2.title: WHERE IS IT CHANGING?
q2.desc: Demarcate verified geographic boundaries across continents, sovereign nations, and administrative sub-regions using authentic coordinate geometries.

q3.title: HOW MUCH IS IT CHANGING?
q3.desc: Compute quantitative rates of change per year and decade using robust Theil-Sen non-parametric median slopes with 95% confidence intervals.

q4.title: HOW STRONG IS THE EVIDENCE?
q4.desc: Test the monotonic trend hypothesis using rank-based Mann-Kendall statistics, reporting standardized Z-scores and exact two-tailed p-values.

lst.name: Land Surface Temperature (LST)
lst.desc: Radiometric thermal emission measured by MODIS Terra sensors, showing thermal energy exchange at the land-atmosphere interface.

rainfall.name: Monthly Precipitation
rainfall.desc: Multi-satellite microwave radiometer and radar calibration from NASA GPM IMERG, tracking monthly surface precipitation accumulation.

ndvi.name: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI)
ndvi.desc: Surface canopy photosynthetic vitality derived from red and near-infrared reflectance ratios.

tws.name: Terrestrial Water Storage Anomaly
tws.desc: Integrated changes in groundwater, soil moisture, and surface reservoirs detected by satellite gravimetry.

solar.name: Surface Solar Irradiance
solar.desc: All-sky surface downward solar flux assimilations from NASA POWER atmospheric and radiation balances.

stats.tsiDisclaimer: Summarizes the strength and directional consistency of observed changes in historical data. Does not establish causality or forecast future state.
stats.insufficientData: Insufficient consecutive observations for a statistically reliable trend estimate.
